rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biology is deeply interconnected with other sciences. Biochemistry studies the chemistry of life (metabolism, enzymes, macromolecules). Biophysics applies physics to biological problems (nerve conduction, muscle mechanics, imaging). Biostatistics uses mathematics in genetics, population models, and experimental design. Geobiology connects biology with earth science (fossils, climate, biogeochemical cycles).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Biochemistry: metabolic pathways (glycolysis, Krebs, ETS) → energy (ATP)
Biophysics: nerve conduction (action potential), muscle mechanics, imaging (MRI)
Biostatistics: Punnett squares, Hardy-Weinberg, population models

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Biochemistry is NOT the same as organic chemistry; it focuses on the chemistry of living systems (metabolism, enzymes, macromolecules).  ·  Biophysics applies physics to biological problems; it is not "physics of life" in a vague sense.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects examples of how biology uses chemistry (biochemistry), physics (biophysics), and mathematics (biostatistics).  ·  Interdisciplinary fields (medicine, agriculture, conservation) are a favourite application question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Biochemistry: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the energy currency of the cell — a molecule studied by chemistry.  ·  Biophysics: nerve conduction involves electrical signals (physics) across the neuron membrane.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Biostatistics is a branch of statistics, not a branch of biology; it is used BY biologists.  ·  Geobiology (biology + earth science) is different from ecology (biology + environment).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Explain biology + chemistry  ·  Explain biology + physics

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Biology = B-I-O (Bio-Interconnected with Other sciences).  ·  Biochem = chemistry of life; Biophys = physics of life; Biostats = math of life.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Explain how biology relates to chemistry.  ·  Describe the role of physics in biology.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Explain how biology relates to chemistry (biochemistry).  ·  Describe the role of physics in biology (biophysics).

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Biochemistry  ·  Biophysics  ·  Biostatistics  ·  Geobiology

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Biology is interconnected with Chemistry, Physics, Mathematics, and Earth Science.  ·  Biochemistry: the chemistry of life (metabolism, enzymes, macromolecules).  ·  Biophysics: physics applied to biology (nerve conduction, muscle, imaging).  ·  Biostatistics: mathematics used in biology (genetics, populations, experiments).

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The DNA double helix was discovered using X-ray crystallography (a physics technique) in 1953.  ·  The electron microscope (physics) revealed cellular structures that light microscopes could not.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: Explain how mathematics is used in biology.  ·  Describe the relationship between biology and earth science.  ·  List three interdisciplinary fields that combine biology with other sciences.

rows.label: More hints
rows.text: Explain how mathematics is used in biology (biostatistics).  ·  List 3 interdisciplinary fields that combine biology with other sciences.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Biostatistics: Mendel's 3:1 ratio (Punnett squares) is a mathematical model of inheritance.  ·  Geobiology: fossil records (earth science) provide evidence for evolution (biology).

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Biochemistry is the study of: → B  ·  The discovery of the DNA double helix used which technique? → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Biology is interconnected with other sciences: it relies on and contributes to Chemistry (biochemistry), Physics (biophysics), Mathematics (biostatistics), and Earth Science (geobiology).  ·  Biochemistry: the chemistry of life — metabolism, enzymes, DNA/RNA/protein structures.  ·  Biophysics: physics applied to biology — biophysics of the cell, nerve conduction, muscle mechanics, imaging (MRI, X-ray).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Punnett squares  ·  The exploration of life science involves knowledge of other basic sciences like Physics and Chemistry.  ·  The combination of these disciplines contributes to a comprehensive perspective.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Relation with Chemistry The physiological processes of plants and animals are intricately linked with chemical reactions.  ·  Biochemistry, situated at the intersection of Biology and Chemistry, is the discipline that addresses this intersection.  ·  Cellular respiration a.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Geobiology: fossil records, biogeochemical cycles, palaeoclimate  ·  Geobiology: interaction of life with Earth (fossils, climate, cycles).  ·  Interdisciplinary fields: medicine, agriculture, conservation, biotechnology.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Biology uses tools from other sciences (microscopes, spectrometers).  ·  Interdisciplinary fields combine multiple sciences; they are NOT a new "fourth" science.  ·  Biology uses tools from other sciences (microscopes, spectrometers) but has its own methods (experiments, observations, classifications).
